description: Two squadrons, one command, and the kind always comes first. Launched mining drones pick their own rocks - nearest ore or ice inside the ship's drone control range, recalling themselves when the hold fills or one of them takes fire - and launched salvage drones work the wrecks around the ship, nearest first or farthest first, going home when the cargo hold fills. /aud mining is the mining menu (on/off, target spread/focus, range, threshold, control, filter, list, status); /aud salvage is the salvage one (on/off, target spread/focus, distance, range, threshold, list, status), and /aud on its own answers with one line per kind of drone without guessing which was meant. Every command has exactly two spellings - its word and one short form of two letters - so /aud mi fl cl ore is /aud mining filter clear ore and /aud sa ds farthest is /aud salvage distance farthest; nothing else is accepted, and what a command takes is always typed in full. A wreck belongs to somebody, but stripping a hull is not what carries a flag in this game, taking the loot is, so every wreck in range is worked. The mining queue is a priority list printed as one numbered list per kind of rock, a mistyped rock name is answered with the one it meant, and /aud copy hands one character's whole setup to another, which is what a multibox fleet wants. Both kinds are classified by the game's own drone effects, so a hull that launches fifty drones under a third-party mod works them all. Every character drives it from ordinary chat (!aud), so no staff rights are needed, and what they choose is saved per character. Server-side only; no client change.
